title: Cooperation, Litigation and Seeing a Case Through
summary: Brings the programme together: criminal referral and parallel proceedings, cooperation with domestic and foreign authorities, giving evidence before tribunals and courts, and feeding outcomes back into supervision.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together: criminal referral and parallel proceedings, cooperation with domestic and foreign authorities, giving evidence before tribunals and courts, and feeding outcomes back into supervision.
Learning Objectives: Decide when criminal referral is appropriate and manage parallel proceedings
Use information-sharing gateways with prosecutors and domestic and foreign authorities
Prepare to give evidence and defend a decision before a tribunal or court
Syllabus: Criminal referral, sequencing and the risk of prejudicing proceedings
Cooperation with police, tax authorities, the national FIU and foreign regulators
Giving evidence, appeals and publication of outcomes
Workshop: taking a case from referral to outcome
Intended Audience: Enforcement investigators, case managers and lawyers
Supervisors who refer cases to enforcement or work alongside enforcement teams
Members of decision-making committees and senior staff responsible for sanctioning and settlement decisions
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervision, investigations or regulatory legal work is helpful. No formal legal qualification is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Credible Deterrence in the Enforcement of Securities Regulation (2015)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
IOSCO, Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MMoU) and Enhanced MMoU (2016)
